audit_findings.title: La Regina dilution is included without La Regina owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: 365.639285 million modeled shares versus 298.206243 million filed shares on June 2, 2026: 67.433042 million, or 22.6%, more shares; denominator-only values would be approximately $20.21 bear, $26.25 base and $29.16 bull before adding La Regina economics
audit_findings.mechanism: The share denominator reduces value per share while the OE numerator, NCI allocation and bridge remain on the pre-acquisition filed perimeter.
audit_findings.evidence: There were 297,992,525 shares of capital stock outstanding as of September 10, 2025.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated date-and-perimeter mismatch. The denominator includes potential La Regina consideration shares, but the $528.6 million anchor contains no La Regina owner earnings. The 22.6% denominator difference is large enough to alter the per-share valuation, although the denominator-only sensitivity is not a corrected valuation because La Regina earnings, NCI and acquisition funding are also missing.
audit_findings.action: Rerun on one post-closing date using actual shares issued, the probable treatment of the $140 million second tranche, La Regina owner earnings attributable to Campbell common equity, the 51% NCI claim and the post-closing cash and debt bridge.

audit_findings.title: Finance-lease asset consumption may escape maintenance capital expenditure
audit_findings.magnitude: FY2025 finance-lease ROU amortization was $29 million and finance-lease ROU additions were $37 million, equal to 5.5% and 7.0% of the $528.6 million anchor, respectively
audit_findings.mechanism: If finance-lease amortization is included in the D&A add-back but finance-lease asset replacement is excluded from maintenance capital expenditure, OE is overstated.
audit_findings.evidence: All operating lease cash payments and interest on finance leases are recorded within Net cash provided by operating activities and all finance lease principal payments are recorded within Net cash used in financing activities in our Consolidated Statements of Cash Flows.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates that finance-lease asset consumption and additions are material relative to the anchor, but the supplied record does not demonstrate whether the OE calculation actually added back the $29 million without an offset. If it did, the mismatch is reasonably capable of changing the near-market base valuation.
audit_findings.action: Trace the $434 million FY2025 depreciation-and-amortization amount used in OE, identify the finance-lease portion added back, and rerun OE with recurring maintenance finance-lease additions or an equivalent asset-use charge.

audit_findings.title: Gross cash may not be entirely excess cash
audit_findings.magnitude: $402 million cash bridge addition, equal to $1.10 per modeled share and 5.1% of base equity value; supplier-finance obligations were $253 million and negative working capital was $395 million at May 3, 2026
audit_findings.mechanism: The bridge adds cash dollar-for-dollar after capitalizing OE; any cash required for operations, seasonal working capital, supplier payments or acquisition funding should not also be treated as excess value.
audit_findings.evidence: Amounts outstanding under these programs, which are included in Accounts payable on the Consolidated Balance Sheets, were $240 million at August 3, 2025, and $243 million at July 28, 2024.
audit_findings.explanation: Adding the entire cash balance is demonstrated, but its excess status is not. The $402 million addition exceeds the $0.03 difference between the $21.41 base value and the $21.38 market price. Supplier-finance obligations are not automatically a cash deduction, but their scale and the negative-working-capital model make an operating-cash assessment material.
audit_findings.action: Determine minimum operating cash from seasonal cash and working-capital history, reconcile the $253 million supplier-finance balance and near-term obligations, incorporate the May 4 La Regina cash payment, and rerun the bridge using only verified excess cash.

audit_findings.title: The latest-year anchor contains offsetting one-offs rather than a normalized annual run rate
audit_findings.magnitude: FY2025 reported after-tax comparability items were a net $290 million adverse, including $131 million of impairment charges, while the 53rd week contributed approximately $0.06 per share, or about $18 million using 300 million diluted shares; anchor OE is $528.6 million
audit_findings.mechanism: Nonrecurring cash and noncash items can distort anchor OE, while the extra week can overstate the annual run rate; the anchor then affects every forecast year and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: There were 53 weeks in 2025 and 52 weeks in 2024 and 2023.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates unusually large offsetting items, but it does not establish that all were mishandled in OE. Impairments may already have been reversed as noncash charges, while transformation and divestiture costs require item-specific treatment. Because the identified items are large relative to the anchor and the base value is essentially equal to market price, the unresolved normalization can change the valuation conclusion in either direction.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the $528.6 million anchor dollar-for-dollar to FY2025 net earnings and cash-flow adjustments, document each comparability item and the 53rd-week adjustment, then rerun only for demonstrated nonrecurring or noncash treatment differences.

audit_findings.title: Future transformation expenditures are not explicitly represented
audit_findings.magnitude: The latest filing estimates $310 million of initiative costs, with $211 million recognized and $99 million remaining; route-optimization expense is capped at $115 million, with $46 million incurred and up to $69 million remaining; planned initiative capital expenditure was $220 million, with $208 million invested
audit_findings.mechanism: Future cash implementation costs and capital spending reduce OE, while realized savings can increase OE or growth; inconsistent timing or double counting affects both explicit forecasts and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: The total estimated pre-tax costs for actions that have been identified to date are approximately $ 215 million, and we expect to incur substantially all of the costs through 2028.
audit_findings.explanation: These are filed, identified programs rather than a generic future risk. Remaining costs of up to $168 million across the two programs are substantial relative to the $528.6 million anchor, but the record does not show how the single growth path treats their timing or related savings. Continuing current charges indefinitely could understate value, while excluding future cash costs or counting savings twice could overstate it.
audit_findings.action: Build an annual schedule through 2029 separating cash costs, noncash charges, capital expenditures and independently supported savings; reconcile benefits already embedded in the anchor before rerunning all scenarios.

audit_findings.evidence: The maximum potential amount of the future payments under existing guarantees we could be required to make is $ 570 million as of August 3, 2025.
audit_findings.explanation: The guarantees are a demonstrated existing exposure, but no material expected loss is demonstrated. The $570 million contractual maximum is not an expected-loss estimate because approximately 4,500 loans are indirectly secured by routes and the recognized liability was not material. The record therefore cannot establish present materiality, but the maximum is too large to dismiss without default and recovery evidence.
